Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business

business noun

trade, dealings, one’s work

also trade, commerce, dealings, do business, on business, business trip, run a business

classical

Cic. Fam. 1.3.1: magna negōtia et ampla et expedīta habet
Traupman 131, 165

negōtium, negōtiī n.

noun, second declension

business, dealings; an affair

Business of every kind, a day’s work or trade: the opposite of ōtium. In the plural, business interests. To run a business, negōtium exercēre (Traupman 131).

Examples

  • cum sē Syrācūsās ōtiandī, nōn negōtiandī causā contulisset

    when he had gone to Syracuse on holiday, not on businessCic. Off. 3.58

  • beātus ille quī procul negōtiīs, ut prīsca gēns mortālium

    happy the man who, far from business, like the first race of men …Hor. Epod. 2.1–2

Other words

  • negōtior, negōtiārī, negōtiātus sum — do business, trade

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 3.58 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. business: do business

  • mercātūra, mercātūrae f. — trade, commerce

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.151: mercātūra autem, sī tenuis est, sordida putanda est (Lewis & Short)

    To be in trade: mercātūrās facere (Cic. Verr. 2.5.72).

  • commercium, commerciī n. — trade, commerce (between peoples)

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Tac. Agr. 24: per commercia et negōtiātōrēs; Liv. 4.52.6 (Lewis & Short)

    Trade as dealings between peoples, and the right to trade (Lewis & Short).

  • negōtiātor, negōtiātōris m. — a businessman, a dealer

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Q. fr. 1.1.7 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 165

See also company, business, job, goods.
